title: Pass named values in a dictionary
summary: A runnable can receive a dictionary when its function expects named fields. This helps keep related inputs together.
introduction: A runnable can receive a dictionary when its function expects named fields. This helps keep related inputs together. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain pass named values in a dictionary
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A runnable can receive a dictionary when its function expects named fields. This helps keep related inputs together.

blocks.code:
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda
label = RunnableLambda(lambda data: data["title"] + " (" + str(data["pages"]) + " pages)")
print(label.invoke({"title": "Moon", "pages": 20}))
blocks.title: Pass named values in a dictionary

blocks.text: The output is Moon (20 pages). The function reads title and pages by key, then joins their text. str changes the number into text.
